date.source: The fed's own tournament story page dates the opening round "War Begins at Sunrise Tomorrow" (21 Oct 2004 entry, sunrise 22 Oct 2004 7:12am EST), running to sunset 29 Oct 2004 (/promotions/ngw/archive/hokori-meiyo-2004-story.html).

notes: A cross-promotion 32-entrant single-elimination tournament NGW hosted on its own site (ngw.theewe.net/tourney/), drawing entrants from a dozen federations plus free agents — see the full entrant list at /promotions/ngw/archive/hokori-meiyo-2004-warriors.html. Judged rather than wrestled: each side submitted up to one roleplay and a panel of judges voted; a side that never submitted anything was ruled a no-show, and a match where BOTH sides no-showed banished both entrants outright rather than advancing either. Round 1 ran 22-29 October 2004: of 16 matches, 8 ended in a double no-show (both entrants banished), 7 were decided by one side no-showing (3-0 judge tally, the opponent advancing by forfeit) and only one (Zidane vs Ty Farrel) was actually judged on its own merits (2-1). Five NGW wrestlers entered this round: Ricky Blaze, Bloody Roar, Reggie Rivid, Kenji Lee and HeartBreak Chick. One of Reggie Rivid's own round-1 opponents is billed only as "Strajk (Free Agent)" — possibly NGW's own National Champion Strajk entering outside his home federation's banner, possibly an unrelated wrestler of the same name from elsewhere in the tournament's dozen federations; not resolved either way, no edge drawn. Matches 1-16 are the whole of round 1; the fed's own numbering resumes at 17 for round 2, served as a separate document.

matches.note: Match 3, Honshu bracket. Lost by forfeit to Emilio Rage (PRIME), 3-0, on a no-show.
Match 5, Hokaido bracket, vs Stoop (XWA). Double no-show — both entrants banished from the tournament.
Match 8, Hokaido bracket, vs Strajk (billed Free Agent, not resolved to a registered id — see show note). Double no-show — both entrants banished from the tournament.
Match 9, Kyushu bracket. Won by forfeit against Chris Vaude (Free Agent), 3-0, on a no-show — advanced to round 2.
Match 13, Shikoku bracket, vs Koji Fujita (Japan). Double no-show — both entrants banished from the tournament.

name: Hokori & Meiyo Tournament — Round 2

date.source: The bracket page's own header: "SUNRISE 30 OCTOBER 2004 (7:12 AM EST) SUNSET 6 NOVEMBER 2004 (6:8 PM EST)" (/promotions/ngw/archive/hokori-meiyo-2004-round-1.html). The served filename reads "round-1" but its own dated header and match numbering (17-24, continuing straight on from round 1's 1-16) place it after round 1 (22-29 October) ended — this is the tournament's second round, mislabeled by filename, not by content.

notes: Round 2 of the Hokori & Meiyo Tournament (see ngw-hokori-meiyo-2004-r1 for the tournament's own format). Only the bracket/card for this round survives — no results page for round 2 was collected, so every appearance below is billed rather than resolved to a match outcome. The round's own bracket pairs each round-1 survivor against a newly-listed entrant not on the original 32-entrant warriors list; the fed's own text calls this 'a reshuffling of the brackets' with 'playins' filling the slots vacated by round 1's double no-shows, though the mechanics of the reshuffle are not fully explained anywhere held. FLAGGED FOR THE COORDINATOR, not resolved here: match 19 (Hokaido bracket) bills "Seymour Almassy" against "John Chernega (Dynasty Wrestling Alliance)", entered under "UWF" — almost certainly the museum's own UWF Seymour Almasy, but the spelling differs by one letter from this wing's own registered form and no edge is drawn here per the no-guessing rule; this identity is held for a separate ruling. Neither side of that match is an NGW entity, so it is not structured into matches[]/appearances[] on this row — recorded here, verbatim, for that reason alone. The three NGW entrants billed this round: John Hitchin (match 17, Honshu bracket, vs Robb Hardy of XWF); Kenji Lee (match 21, Kyushu bracket, vs Doomsday of Extreme Wrestling Federation — a different, unrelated character from this wing's own newly-minted doomsday-ngw, per that entrant's own EWF billing); and Dallas Reeves (match 24, Shikoku bracket, vs Josh Sutton of Chaos Heat Zone, the same Josh Sutton who advanced out of round 1's match 16). No round-2 results page survives for any of the three.
